New Release

The Gentle Art of Dying Upside Down

On the Dignity of Endurance

We are culturally taught that to survive, we must hold on tight. But what if holding on is just exhaustion in disguise? This book explores the concept of the “passive grip”—how bats hang effortlessly in the dark, only using energy when it’s time to fly.

Through nature writing and deeply human stories—a daughter peeling an apple for her mother fading into dementia, a mother packing gifts for a daughter she will not live to see grow up—the book offers a comforting perspective on mortality: that endings are not failures, but arrivals. It’s a companion for anyone navigating grief, caregiving, or a major life transition.

Arnie Rose

Author of The Gentle Art of Dying Upside Down and the You Were Never series. Her recent literary collections, including Ode to Home: Letters of the Living and The Good Minute, serve as companion works to her new book. Her next book, The Confessions of an Optimist: I Hate Being Human, is forthcoming. Beyond her literary work, she develops educational resources in project management and supply chain management.
